Operation Midnight Frost: a spearphishing campaign against European ministries

Cozy Bear sent spearphishing emails with a malicious attachment from alerts@mail-notice-ministry.test to staff of foreign ministries in Germany and Poland. The campaign, tracked as Midnight Frost, targeted the government sector and the energy sector.

The attachment dropped a loader called SUNBURST. After execution SUNBURST created the mutex Global\MidnightFrostMtx and wrote a persistence entry under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\FrostSvc. The loader also dropped the file svchost_update.dll, identified by the hashes 3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301 (MD5) and e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 (SHA-256).

SUNBURST contacted the command-and-control server at 91.215.85.17 and resolved frostmail-cdn.test for its second stage, downloaded from http://frostmail-cdn.test/stage/payload.bin. The operators used PowerShell to run commands on the compromised hosts. Cozy Bear dumped credentials from LSASS memory with Mimikatz.

The intrusion exploited CVE-2023-23397 in Microsoft Outlook to steal NTLM hashes before the attachment was opened. Defenders should block frostmail-cdn.test at the proxy and hunt for the registry key above.
